design_notes: The table has Cost, Days and Effect columns and no Strengths or Drawbacks. Each cell is shown as a strength when it helps the team and as a drawback when it hurts, with the column name in front ("Cost −15% total"). Standard has none.
The "Fact" column is stored in twin. F01 (Mars Climate Orbiter) is attached to "Faster, Cheaper" because its fact line names that loss; the bank ties F01 to MG-01.
Cost and Days are relative modifiers on cost_M and schedule_days for the whole mission ("−15% total"). The design does not say whether launch site fees, tests and anomaly costs are inside "total".

"Uncertainty bands ×1.5" and "×0.5" are multipliers on uncertainty_band of all parts. The design's "+1% reliability on all parts" (7.20) would be +0.01, read as percentage points (README, open question 9); the data uses +0.005 as a balance change (see assur_class_a design_notes).
No option is restricted to a contract. No model path: an assurance level is a way of working, not a piece of the rocket.

Decision (T012 balance fix, game_value): the reliability bonus is +0.005 (+0.5 percentage points on every part), half the +1% of design 7.20. The T012 balance report found that with +0.01 the safest build of 8 of 9 contracts reached at least 99.9% displayed success only through this bonus, which lifts most parts to the 99.99% cap, so the expensive-and-safe archetype looked the same everywhere (for example C1 97.52% without it, 99.96% with it). Halving it keeps the cost/schedule versus reliability trade-off visible. Design 7.20 and section 19 should be updated if the change is kept after playtest.
